I've posted before what I personally think their angle is; so here goes.

I think their plan is three-fold.

First and foremost Windows retail users have (at least since XP days) never bought Retail copies of any OS in any volume. Sure it was there, but no one lined up to buy any of them. Their major sources of OS licensing was/is primarily OEM's and businesses. So their angle is, they are selling 10 Enterprise on a bunch of new features and controls and the fact that patches will be 'tried out' on home/volunteer users before hitting Enterprise.

Two; why give away 10? Dovetails nicely into the whole idea of getting guinea pigs for Corp users, but that's the icing on the cake. The cake is the Windows Store. They see the Google's and Apples of the world raking in money selling other people's apps. They baked in Windows Store, they are pushing live tiles out with ads for services and they are 'charging' for Solitaire to prove that there is a market. They also are open-sourcing .net and making 10 android friendly so-as-to be able to sell apps.

Third; Cortana is their logical answer to Google Now and Siri. They're trying to keep up with the times (hell even Amazon beat them to the punch with their home device) and secondarily build a bigger market for Bing ad network(which I'm sure is still seriously struggling). Also if you really want to use Cortana you need to utilize their Mail/Calendar/etc services, which also gives them more ad-views.

TL;DR Home users were never the money makers in the past, give away 10 to sell people apps in the Store, and finally give Bing ads a boost by offering people Cortana.
